name: Staff Wellbeing, Time, and Retention
title: Staff Wellbeing, Time, and Retention
answer: This idea is that AI's promise to reduce teacher workload only helps staff wellbeing and retention when schools audit the time saved and decide, with teachers, where that time goes. It also covers using staff surveys and retention analysis carefully, with feedback loops and support rather than punishment. It matters because burnout and turnover are serious problems and workload is a major cause, yet saved time can vanish and data can damage trust if it is not governed.

sections.body: Teacher burnout and turnover are serious problems, and workload is a major cause. AI has been promoted as a way to reduce workload, but the evidence is mixed. The idea is to make time savings real through a time savings audit tied to reinvestment, with a written decision made with teachers about where saved time goes. It also includes staff surveys that reveal morale, workload, and concerns, and retention analysis that identifies staff who may be at risk of leaving. The problem it solves is that without these decisions and safeguards, saved time disappears and staff data can be used in ways that harm trust.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, leaders can run a simple time study and then decide with teachers where the saved time will go, recording that decision so the savings are not absorbed by other demands. Staff surveys can use AI features to group open responses into themes, with a staff member checking the grouping. Leaders should share the results with staff along with the actions they will take. Retention analysis can help leaders see which staff may be at risk of leaving, and any support offered might include mentoring, a schedule change, or a conversation. The text does not set out separate grade bands, though it cites a primary school study.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book describes the evidence as mixed. A primary school study found planning time cut by more than half, but the saved time was absorbed by other demands (Carson et al., 2026). A review of automatic feedback found that nearly half of studies showed no reduction in instructor workload (Cavalcanti et al., 2021). This means AI workload relief is not guaranteed and must be checked in the school's own setting.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Retention analysis must be used only to offer support, such as mentoring, a schedule change, or a conversation. It must never be used to make decisions about contracts or assignments. Staff should know how this data is used. Surveys that lead nowhere discourage honest answers, so results should be shared with staff along with the actions leaders will take. AI grouping of open responses needs a staff member to check the grouping, and without a written decision about where saved time goes, saved time disappears.
